title: Capacity control after growth
summary: A deterministic XOR checkpoint comparing freeze, fine-tune, and prune policies after one hidden-unit insertion.
learning_objectives: Compare three post-insertion policies from the same grown-network checkpoint.
Distinguish preserving established features from fine-tuning the full network.
Observe that deleting capacity can worsen fit even when a curvature-inspired proxy ranks the deletion first.
Treat growth and pruning as capacity-control choices rather than assuming that more neurons are always better.
limitations: The XOR schedule and group proxy are pinned demonstration choices, not paper reproductions.
The pruning proxy is OBD-inspired but omits the full parameter Hessian; it is neither OBD nor OBS.
Reed's survey PDF is image-only in the local extraction path, so it grounds the survey role rather than mechanism details.
The cited GPSNN uses spiking neurons, latency, dominance, and a two-stage procedure; this sigmoid XOR network does not reproduce it.
